entry.title: Lido Lend Plan Would Block Repayments, Not Interest
entry.summary: A proposed emergency pause would also stop lender exits and liquidations. A separate governance mechanism could remove its automatic expiry.

entry.summary: Luigi D'Onorio DeMeo reported about $18 million for one day and $21 million so far the next.

entry.summary: Bitcoin and ether rebounded after another sharp drop, but matched 24-hour windows show the selloff accelerated from the Nov. 12 break below $72,000.

entry.summary: CoinGlass recorded $2.05 billion in liquidations across tracked exchanges, overwhelmingly in bets on rising prices.

entry.summary: Coinbase and Bitstamp both recorded the break. Bitcoin's new low was 12.5% below the snapshot low in The Defiant's Nov. 12 report.

entry.summary: A Bot API contributor confirmed that general bots cannot send HTML widgets, including in private chats. The restriction is narrower than a freeze on all mini-apps.

entry.summary: The slide has deepened since the Nov. 12 break below $72,000. A SpaceX IPO comparison offers a bullish scenario, not proof that selling is nearly over.

entry.summary: Inflated BUSD collateral let attackers borrow 55.2 million KAVA. Bridge withdrawals and transfers at three Korean exchanges were suspended.

entry.summary: The upper-stage recovery brings SpaceX closer to reusing both parts of its launch system. Super Heavy, however, diverted to an offshore splashdown.

entry.title: Who Sells Shares When a Stock Leaves a Market Index?
entry.summary: An index change can prompt tracking funds to sell shares. That is different from exchange delisting—or a bitcoin-holding company selling its coins.

entry.title: Pennysia Users Urged to Revoke Approvals After Exploit
entry.summary: Onchain records show swaps were disabled before SlowMist's public warning. The cited drain affected four addresses.

entry.summary: Shi Bingzhe and two companies face money-laundering allegations over purchases of 917 servers, expanding a probe involving shipments to Malaysia.

entry.summary: Up to 5,000 users potentially received a tampered Claude Code extension. Cursor is urging affected teams to check machines and rotate exposed credentials.

entry.title: 1inch Warns Delegators to Claim Rewards by Nov. 27
entry.summary: New resolver delegations are closed. Existing delegators should claim rewards and undelegate before the deadline; plain 1INCH staking is unaffected.

entry.summary: An independent open letter seeks Huang's reinstatement, but its signature tally is not identity-verified and the board has announced no reversal.

entry.summary: The report identifies Rubio's role in the warning that preceded Jensen Huang's exit, but does not resolve the espionage allegation or establish that he invented it.

entry.summary: The planned Solana integration would fund lender returns with covered calls, leaving borrowers exposed to forgone gains and liquidation.

entry.summary: Proposal 1061 is above quorum with near-unanimous support. Validators would need Gaia v29.1.0 at block 33,935,300 if it passes.

entry.summary: Developers dropped quick slots but left FOCIL and a new consensus direction unresolved. Christine D. Kim described development as 'on pause.'

entry.summary: The European service supports bitcoin, ether and three stablecoins. Stablecoin conversion and tokenized financial instruments remain later steps.

entry.summary: Some investors are exploring offshore bids, Bloomberg reports, but receiving shares remains uncertain ahead of expected Nov. 18 pricing.

entry.summary: The FAA announced SMART’s expansion to airspace covered by 22 centers on Nov. 10. Duffy blamed overloaded legacy telecom equipment for Friday’s halt.

entry.summary: OpenAI says it investigated and took preventive action, without detailing changes to how it verifies government contacts.

entry.summary: Eligible clients can seek share-backed ANTx tokens, not direct stock ownership. Requests reserve funds and may receive no allocation.

entry.summary: Huang is asked to appear Dec. 3 and Lutnick Dec. 10. A Commerce spokesperson says the secretary has agreed to testify voluntarily.

entry.summary: Northwestern Polytechnical reportedly bought two Nvidia accelerators through a Chinese supplier, despite restrictions that survived January's easing of H200 export licensing.

entry.summary: The lawmaker's account contrasts with a semiconductor trade group's warning about mandatory safeguards on advanced AI chips.
